text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said on Friday that it confirmed its ratings for Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd after news of a major acquisition in France.
The rating agency said that Fairfax's senior unsecured long term debt was confirmed at BBB (high) with a stable trend.

Fairfax said earlier today that it agreed to acquire Compagnie Transcontinentale de Reassurance, the reinsurance unit of French insurer GAN. The deal was valued at 700 million francs (US$137.9 million).
Shares in the Toronto-based financial services company soared after the deal was announced. Fairfax stock was up 27 at 225, a new high, in turnover of 73,000 shares.

The GAN deal was the latest recent acquisition by Fairfax and raised concerns at DBRS about over-expansion. The agency said Fairfax's move into reinsurance would also raise its risk profile compared to the company's traditional property and casualty operations.
But DBRS said it confirmed Fairfax's ratings for a number of reasons, including the fact that the acquisition price was well below book value.
DBRS said Fairfax's plan to issue common equity would ensure that the company's capital ratios and liquidity levels were not weakened.
Fairfax plans to finance the purchase by drawing on a 10-year 300 million franc credit facility and by issuing more subordinate voting shares.
DBRS said the French company's recent performance and management also appeared to be satisfactory.
